subject: NorthPoint cluster intake - node pools, storage & networking checklist
messages:
From: Rajesh Mehra <r.mehra@northpointhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Christine Lopez <c.lopez@northpointhealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: NorthPoint private cluster intake: node inventory & storage questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the quick overview of Redwood Private. We need to start the intake for our planned on-prem cluster (NorthPoint Regional Data Center #3). To get alignment with our infra and procurement teams, can you send a concise checklist of required cluster inventory items and the storage expectations you recommend for our workload (LLM inference, medium seq lengths, KV-cache hotset)?

Specific asks from our side:
- A node inventory template (CPU, GPU model, disk types and sizes, NICs) we can fill and return.
- Guidance on node pool separation: control-plane vs. inference vs. batch/eviction nodes.
- Recommended PV classes and encryption/backup constraints.
- Any prescriptive networking requirements (VLAN tags, egress rules for telemetry, NTP/DNS lock-down) for Private deployments.
- A ballpark timeline for an initial 3-node inference pool + 1 control/infra node (procurement lead asked for ETA to schedule shipping).

We also need to know what evidence/data we should prepare for your security review (audit logs, SOC2 scoping questions).

Can you loop in whoever should own the technical intake? I’ve CC’d Christine who will coordinate on our side.

Best,
Rajesh
Director of Platform Engineering
NorthPoint Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
To: Rajesh Mehra <r.mehra@northpointhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood-inference.com>, Christine Lopez <c.lopez@northpointhealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NorthPoint private cluster intake: node inventory & storage questions

Hi Rajesh — thanks for the clear list. I’ve pulled together a compact intake pack and a node-inventory template for your procurement/field teams to complete. Attached: NP_node_inventory_template.xlsx and a short Redwood on-prem playbook (redwood_onprem_playbook_v1.pdf) that covers the standard nodepool split and networking defaults.

High-level answers inline:
- Node inventory template: attached. Please list NIC model, PCIe lanes to GPU, local NVMe sizing and whether you intend to use separate blockstore (SAN) for inference checkpoints.
- Node pools: our recommended starter layout for LLM inference workloads is:
  * control-plane (3 control-plane VMs for etcd/leader election; can be small CPU-only)
  * infra/ops (1-2 nodes for logging, metrics, CSI controller)
  * inference pool (3 dedicated GPU nodes for steady-state inference; homogeneous GPU family recommended)
  * burst/batch pool (optional; cheaper GPU flavor or CPU-backed batch workers)
- PV classes: use a fast NVMe localVolume class for KV hotset and an encrypted blockstore class (iSCSI/Ceph/RBD) for checkpoints/backups. We recommend LUKS + KMS for at-rest encryption; document in the intake whether you require HSM-backed keys.
- Networking: allow outbound TLS to telemetry.redwood-inference.com on 443; tag a dedicated VLAN for control/data traffic; ensure BGP connectivity only for failover (if applicable). Time sync (NTP) and DNS should be resolvable from the cluster; we provide a checklist of required ports in the playbook.
- Timeline: once the completed inventory is back and procurement confirms shipping, field prep + image bake typically takes 2–3 weeks; initial 3-node inference pool + control/infra validation + on-site runbook handoff is usually a 4–6 week cadence depending on shipping lead times.

Security/evidence: we’ll need the facility SOC contact, network ACLs for the proposed VLAN, and confirmation of KMS/HSM choice for keys. I’ll have Marissa and Karthik reach out with a short preflight questionnaire for SOC2-relevant items.

Next steps:
1) Please return the filled NP_node_inventory_template.xlsx — procurement can attach shipping ETA.
2) We’ll schedule a 30-min intake tech review with our field engineering (Marissa) after we have the inventory.

Attaching the template and playbook now.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com
[Attachment: NP_node_inventory_template.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]
[Attachment: redwood_onprem_playbook_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood-inference.com>, Christine Lopez <c.lopez@northpointhealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NorthPoint private cluster intake: node inventory & storage questions

Rajesh — adding a few implementation-level notes that help with storage sizing and nodepool behavior (brief):

1) Inference node sizing: for medium sequence LLMs we typically recommend GPU families with >=48GB VRAM for the steady-state nodes (NVIDIA A40 / equivalent). If you plan to use quantized weights (int8/4bit) later, we can support smaller-GPU instance families but will want homogenous firmware/drivers across pool.

2) Local NVMe vs network blockstore:
  - KV hotset on local NVMe (use at least 2 NVMe devices striped for redundancy or use RAID1 to prevent single-disk eviction issues).
  - Checkpoints: store on network blockstore with scheduled snapshotting to an offsite backup (we can help configure the snapshot cadence).

3) Eviction and QoS: label inference pods with nodeAffinity to prevent eviction from burst nodes; reserve CPU and memory on inference nodes to keep runtime stable. If using cgroup v2, lock the scheduler reservations explicitly.

4) CSI and driver notes: prefer CSI drivers that support volume health probes and multi-attach if you plan to failover active checkpoints. We have a supported CSI list in the playbook.

5) Operational checklist (short):
  - Validate MTU across VLANs to avoid packet fragmentation for large KV transfers.
  - Confirm IPMI/remote-console access for field images.
  - Test time sync and verify NTP stratum stability.

I’ve attached a one-page runbook snippet for the 3-node validation steps (runbook_snippet.txt) and a small sample nodepool config that maps required labels/taints. Please let us know if NorthPoint has a preferred GPU vendor or procurement constraints—procurement ETA will change choice of rackable chassis/cooling requirements.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Field Engineering, Redwood Inference
